issues.t: Death wobble front-end shake
issues.sym: After hitting a bump at speed, the steering wheel and front end shake violently and do not stop until you slow way down.
issues.why: The solid front axle depends on tight steering and suspension parts. Worn or loose track bar bolts and bushings, tie rods, ball joints or a weak steering damper can start a runaway shake. On 2018-2019 models Jeep offered a redesigned steering damper.
issues.next: Slow down firmly without jerking the wheel. Have the track bar, its bolts and mounts, tie rods, ball joints and steering damper inspected and tightened or replaced before driving at speed again.

issues.t: Oil leaks from rear main seal, valve cover and oil pan
issues.sym: Oil spots under the Jeep, oil on the bottom of the engine or transmission bellhousing, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: The 4.0L commonly leaks at the two-piece rear main seal, the valve cover gasket, the oil pan gasket and the timing cover. The steel oil pan can also rust through from the inside.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the oil level and have the leak traced to its source. Fix leaks that drip onto the exhaust promptly.

issues.t: Radiator leaks where the plastic tank meets the core
issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the Jeep, a sweet smell, a dropping coolant level, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The factory radiator uses plastic end tanks crimped onto the core, and the seam can separate and leak. The 4.0L also makes a lot of heat for the stock radiator.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and coolant level. Replace a leaking radiator before it causes overheating.

issues.t: Frame rust, especially near the rear suspension mounts
issues.sym: Flaking or swollen frame rails, holes near the rear wheel area, clunks from the rear suspension, or soft spots in the floor.
issues.why: The frame tends to rot from the inside, often starting above the rear wheels near the lower suspension arm mounts. The front floorboards also rust.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected, especially before buying. Serious rot at suspension mounts makes the Jeep unsafe to drive until repaired.

issues.t: Water leaks into the cab
issues.sym: Wet carpet or floor after rain or a car wash, a musty smell, or water dripping near the windshield corners.
issues.why: Water can get past the A-pillar seals and, on early models, through the windshield cowl vent. Revised seals and a later cowl design reduced it.
issues.next: Find and reseal the leak soon. Lift wet carpet to dry it, since standing water rusts the floor.

issues.t: Axle pinion seal and transfer case leaks
issues.sym: Gear oil wetting the front or rear axle where the driveshaft connects, or fluid seeping from the middle of the transfer case.
issues.why: The axle pinion seals commonly leak, and the transfer case halves are sealed only with sealant, which can seep over time. Front axle shaft U-joints also wear.
issues.next: Check the axle and transfer case fluid levels and have leaking seals replaced before the gears run low on oil.

issues.t: Vehicle may roll away in Park (recall 05V-460)
issues.sym: The Jeep creeps or rolls after being shifted into Park, especially on a slope.
issues.why: A cup plug inside the automatic transmission can come loose and keep the park mechanism from holding.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check the VIN for the recall right away.

issues.t: Fuel spills back out of the filler while refueling
issues.sym: Gas spits or overflows out of the filler neck at the pump, and the nozzle does not click off in time.
issues.why: The fuel filler and tank venting do not take fuel smoothly, so fuel backs up the filler neck. It is the most reported complaint for this year.
issues.next: Fill slowly at a lower nozzle speed and stop at the first click. Have the filler and vent system checked if fuel keeps spilling.

issues.t: Fuse box module (TIPM) causes odd electrical faults
issues.sym: Hard starting or no start, the fuel pump not running, or random problems with the horn, wipers, turn signals or lights.
issues.why: The integrated power module that houses many fuses and relays can develop internal faults.
issues.next: Have a shop test the module before replacing other parts. Repaired or updated modules are available.

issues.t: Airbag light from steering wheel clockspring (recall 16V-290)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on, and the horn or steering wheel buttons may work only sometimes.
issues.why: Dust can contaminate the coiled wiring inside the steering column and break the airbag circuit.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. An airbag light means the driver airbag may not deploy in a crash.

issues.t: Left cylinder head valve seat problem (warranty extension)
issues.sym: A ticking noise from the engine, a rough idle or misfire, and a check engine light, usually pointing to cylinder 2.
issues.why: A valve seat in the left cylinder head could wear or loosen on some early Pentastar engines. Chrysler extended the warranty on the left head for affected vehicles.
issues.next: Have the misfire diagnosed soon and ask the dealer whether the head warranty extension applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Cracked oil filter and cooler housing
issues.sym: Oil leaking at the top back of the engine, a burning oil smell, coolant loss, or oil and coolant mixing in the reservoir.
issues.why: The plastic housing that holds the oil filter and oil cooler can crack from repeated heat cycles.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and replace the housing with an updated part. Do not let oil drip onto hot exhaust parts.

issues.t: Transmission cooler line can leak (recall 13V-234)
issues.sym: Red fluid dripping under the Jeep, a burning smell, or smoke from underneath.
issues.why: A transmission oil cooler line could leak fluid onto hot exhaust parts and start a fire under the vehicle.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. If you see fluid dripping or smell burning, stop and have it towed for repair.

issues.t: Front track bar bracket weld (recall 18V-675)
issues.sym: Wandering or delayed steering, a clunk from the driver-side front frame area, or a visible crack at the bracket.
issues.why: Some brackets that hold the front track bar to the frame were not welded properly and can separate.
issues.next: Check for open recalls by VIN and avoid off-road use until it is inspected.

issues.t: Loose, wandering steering from the steering gear (TSBs)
issues.sym: Play or a dead spot at center, constant small corrections on the highway, or steering that briefly goes heavy in cold weather.
issues.why: The original aluminum steering gear could develop play, and the power steering pump calibration could lose assist in the cold. Jeep released a steel replacement gear and a software update.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about the steering gear bulletins and have the steering checked before the play gets worse.

issues.t: Manual clutch overheating (recalls)
issues.sym: A clutch overheat warning, a burning smell after slow off-road or stop-and-go driving, or slipping or juddering when taking off.
issues.why: The clutch pressure plate can overheat and in some cases break apart, risking fire, debris or loss of drive. Recalls added software and, later, a new clutch.
issues.next: Check recall status. If you see the warning or smell burning, stop and let the clutch cool.

issues.t: Shifter shows Park when not locked (recall 18V-280)
issues.sym: The Jeep rolls after the shifter is placed in Park.
issues.why: Some early vehicles got an incorrect park-lock rod, so the transmission may not lock even though Park is displayed.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check the VIN for the recall right away.

issues.t: Cruise control may not cancel (recall 18V-332)
issues.sym: Cruise control keeps the vehicle accelerating or holding speed after you try to cancel it.
issues.why: A software problem could keep cruise control from disengaging.
issues.next: Do not use cruise control until the VIN is checked and the recall software is installed.

issues.t: 8-speed shift problems and shudder (TSB)
issues.sym: Harsh or missed shifts, a shudder, the transmission not shifting, or a check engine light with gear ratio codes.
issues.why: Jeep issued a service bulletin for gear ratio fault codes and shift complaints on this transmission.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer about the bulletin and any software update.

issues.t: Coolant leak at the water pump inlet (TSB)
issues.sym: A dropping coolant level, a sweet smell, or coolant residue near the front of the engine.
issues.why: Jeep issued bulletins for coolant leaks at the water pump and its inlet tube fasteners.
issues.next: Top off with the correct coolant and have the leak checked before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Instrument cluster can go blank (recall 24V-652)
issues.sym: The gauge cluster display goes dark, hiding speed and warning lights.
issues.why: An internal short circuit in the instrument cluster can shut off the display.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. Drive with care until fixed, since warnings may not show.

issues.t: Fuel supply line connector can crack (recall 21V-665)
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell from the engine bay or a visible fuel leak.
issues.why: A connector near the high-pressure fuel pump can crack and leak gasoline onto the engine.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, stop driving and have the Jeep inspected. Check the VIN for the recall.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump failure (recalls)
issues.sym: Hard starting, stalling, loss of power, or fuel pressure warning codes.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel pump can fail and send debris into the fuel system, stalling the engine.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recalls. If the engine stalls or loses power, get off the road and have it towed.

issues.t: 4xe high-voltage battery fire risk (recalls)
issues.sym: Usually no warning beforehand. Some vehicles show hybrid or battery warnings.
issues.why: The high-voltage battery can fail internally and catch fire, whether parked or driving. Later recalls replaced earlier software fixes.
issues.next: Look up your VIN. Until repaired, follow the recall instructions, which have included not charging and parking outdoors.

issues.t: 4xe engine debris can cause engine failure (recall 25V-766)
issues.sym: Knocking or rough running, a check engine light and reduced power.
issues.why: Debris left inside the engine can damage it, causing loss of drive power or an engine-bay fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. Stop driving if the engine knocks or loses power.

issues.t: Power steering pump wiring fire risk (recall 26V-363)
issues.sym: A burning smell from the front of the engine bay, a power steering warning, or heavy steering.
issues.why: Wiring to the electric-hydraulic power steering pump can overheat and start a fire, even with the Jeep turned off.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and park outside, away from buildings, until it is repaired.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning light may not work (recall 25V-527)
issues.sym: The tire pressure warning light fails to come on when a tire is low.
issues.why: A pinched remote-start antenna wire can keep the tire pressure warning light from working properly.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and check tire pressures by hand until it is fixed.

issues.t: Steel wheels can crack (recall 26V-456)
issues.sym: A vibration, a wheel that will not hold air, or visible cracks in the wheel.
issues.why: Some steel wheels were made with walls that are too thin and may crack or come off.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall right away and do not drive on a cracked wheel.
